title: SDK intake: multi-language client + auth streaming ergonomics for enterprise
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Intake ticket for a set of customer requests aggregated during Q1 enterprise outreach: multi-language SDK support (Java, .NET, Go), a standardized token/profile-based auth pattern for private deployments, and improved streaming ergonomics (client-side backpressure, reconnect semantics, cancelation). Goal: triage, prioritize, and produce a minimal design + implementation plan for the next SDK release cycle. Scope excludes breaking API surface changes to hosted API; this is client-side SDK ergonomics and auth wrappers for Private/Dedicated customers.
requests_summary: Large enterprise customers (FinServCorp, HealthGrid, Acme Ads) requested first-class Java and .NET SDKs with idiomatic streaming APIs.
Security teams asked for a standard auth pattern supporting KMS-backed service credentials and short-lived tokens suitable for private deployments (VPC) and HSM integrations.

Platform engineering asked for a single streaming primitive across SDKs that supports client-controlled backpressure, reconnect with resume via KV-cache-compatible tokens, and clear cancelation semantics for CLI and server use-cases.
Telemetry/observability hooks in SDKs (trace propagation, token usage metrics) requested by platform teams for cost breakdown and latency attribution.
prioritization_rationale: High customer impact and multiple enterprise customers converging on the same asks -> prioritize. Dependencies on runtime (ENG-2891: streaming resume protocol) and infra (ENG-2940: auth token exchange service) mean we must coordinate. Short-term priority is to stabilize an auth pattern and deliver idiomatic Java/.NET streaming clients; longer-term plan includes Go and improved telemetry. Trade-offs: building first-class SDKs increases maintenance cost but reduces onboarding friction and support burden for enterprise customers.
triage_decision: 1) Prioritize Java and .NET SDKs for the next release (sdk-1.8) as P0 deliverables. 2) Implement a standardized auth facade: short-lived signed tokens + optional KMS/HSM exchange flow (design required). 3) Define streaming ergonomics spec (single primitive) and implement client-side backpressure and resumable streams in runtime coordination with ENG-2891. 4) Defer full Go SDK to next cycle after initial spec validates. 5) Add telemetry hooks as non-blocking instrumentation work.
acceptance_criteria: Java and .NET SDKs provide createClient(), authenticateWithKms(), openStream() with backpressure API, and example apps (token refresh demo).
Auth facade design doc approved and security review completed for Private deployments.
Streaming spec includes resume token format, reconnect behavior, and cancellation semantics; validated against ENG-2891 test harness.
Integration test suite demonstrating end-to-end auth exchange (KMS flow), streaming resume, and trace propagation.
Documentation and quickstart notebooks for enterprise onboarding included in SDK repo.
implementation_notes: Consider exposing a small surface in all SDKs that maps to runtime capabilities instead of re-implementing streaming state machines per language.

Auth pattern proposal: short-lived JWT signed by customer-managed KMS; exchange service returns ephemeral session token scoped to model+route; SDKs auto-refresh via provided callback. See design draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDK/Auth+Facade+Draft
Streaming ergonomics: prefer push-pull iterator pattern for Java, IAsyncEnumerable for .NET; expose high-level helpers (batching, retry, backpressure) and low-level raw stream for power users.
Telemetry: add optional TraceProvider interface in SDKs so customers can plug OpenTelemetry. Do not hard-require instrumentation to avoid dependency bloat.
updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created after PM readout of enterprise requests from Field Eng and AE team. Attached initial customer ask bundle.
2026-03-03: Interviewed FinServCorp security lead; clarified requirement for HSM-backed signing and ability to rotate signing keys without SDK redeploy.

2026-03-05: Engineering sync with ENG leads (runtime + infra). ENG-2891 scoped as streaming resume implementation; ENG-2940 scoped as token exchange service. Both dependencies identified as critical path.
2026-03-08: Design review scheduled. Preliminary auth facade doc posted; Security requested threat model and key rotation diagram.
2026-03-10: PM/Design alignment: prefer idiomatic language surfaces over one-size-fits-all bindings. Decided Java/.NET prioritized; Go deferred.
2026-03-11: Added acceptance criteria and requested estimate (5 pts). Assigned to Ethan Kim for coordination with ENG owners.
notes_for_engineering: Coordinate with ENG-2891 for compatible resume token format; design must include token revocation semantics and minimal server-side state.
Keep SDK dependencies small; prefer optional plumbing packages for telemetry to avoid transitive conflicts in enterprise codebases.
Plan a small compatibility shim so customers can adopt new auth flow incrementally (opt-in) to avoid breaking on-prem deployments.
